items.title: NextEra Energy (NEE) Draws Fresh Virginia Questions Over Merger Consumer Protections
items.summary: NextEra Energy (NYSE:NEE) faces fresh scrutiny as Virginia's Consumer Counsel flags ongoing gaps in the merger case with Dominion Energy. The Consumer Counsel's latest regulatory filing questions the completeness of merger data on competitive effects, rate impacts, and consumer safeguards. Regulators in Virginia are being asked to examine alleged filing errors, unclear market impact assumptions, and the enforceability of promised protections for customers. items.title: AI Boom Fuels Southern Company's Data Center Power Usage Growth
items.summary: SO's data center electricity usage surges 59% in Q3 2026, backed by 21 GW of signed contracts, fueling growth and major capital investment plans.

items.title: What Are Wall Street Analysts' Target Price for Dominion Energy Stock?
items.summary: Despite lagging the S&P 500 over the past year, Dominion Energy continues to face a measured outlook from Wall Street analysts, reflecting lingering caution about its growth prospects.

items.title: People Pay the Power Bill Before Almost Anything Else. $45,000 in Each of These 3 Utilities Pays $5,915 a Year
items.summary: When money gets tight, Netflix and dinners out get cut long before the electric bill. Three regulated utilities turn that habit into dividend income, but a pending merger, a wildfire threat, and share dilution complicate the picture.

items.title: NextEra Energy vs. Southern Company: Which Dividend Stock Is Better for Retirement?
items.summary: Both utilities just beat earnings estimates and both are cashing in on data center demand. But one has faster growth while the other has the steadier paycheck, and retirees have to decide which of those matters more.

items.title: Western Union Yields 13.5%. Is This Dividend Stock a Trap?
items.summary: The payout hasn't moved in years, yet the yield keeps climbing because investors keep dumping the stock. We tested three high-yield names on earnings, cash flow, and debt, and one of them is paying dividends from reserves.

items.title: NextEra Energy Vs. AES Corporation: Utility Scale Energy Production Just Got a Major Blue Boost
items.summary: Democrats just took Congress, and clean energy stocks surged. But one utility giant is racing to build batteries for data centers while its rival has already put itself up for sale. Only one of them captured the rally.
